title: Three Weeks and One Short Envelope
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：post　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 post 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1980 the postman ① kept the post that no sender in the office would have noted, and he said the keeping was the whole of the week. The ② post, meaning the office itself and not the envelope, ran three weeks and stayed unnoted in the book; a post, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ post in that office had the same short envelope beside it, and the ④ post at the far box, meaning the parcel they kept for the children to fetch and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A post, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the postman said the noting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the post was the whole of the matter, meaning the duty and not the office. The ⑥ post, meaning the duty and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; post, he said, is either something you keep or the only word that means both an office and a duty. He said the duty is the part they remember.

By 1985 the ⑦ post had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short envelope. The ⑧ post of the whole thing, the postman wrote in June, was one office and three weeks of noting; post, he said, is either the parcel at the far box or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ post I remember is the office noted in the list, which closed in 1987 and is still noted as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ post, my mother said in 1989, is the only office that improves by being noted; every post, she said, is a duty that has agreed to look like an office. She said the duty was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 邮政；岗位（指邮局里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 邮政；岗位（指那个邮政本身，与薄薄的信封相对）
C. 固定搭配：keep the post 守这一个邮政
D. n. 邮政；岗位（指留给孩子们取的那一件）
E. n. 邮政之事（抽象总称，指一处邮局的邮政之事）
F. n. 邮政；岗位（指收发清单里写到、被记下的那一个）
G. n. 邮政、职守（指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 职守（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: kept the post that no sender in the office would have noted
The post, meaning the office itself and not the envelope
the post at the far box
the post was the whole of the matter
the post had become a line in a list
The post of the whole thing
A post, my mother said in 1989

answers.why: keep the post 意为“守这一个邮政”，1980 年那位邮差把邮局里没有一位寄信人肯记下的一个邮政做了一遍。
post 意为“邮政；岗位”，指那个邮政本身而不是薄薄的信封，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记下。
post 意为“邮政；岗位”，指邮局里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一个薄薄的信封。
post 意为“邮政；岗位”，指最远那只信箱的留给孩子们取的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
post 意为“邮政、职守”，指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个职守就是那件事的全部。
post 意为“职守”，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个邮政，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
post 意为“邮政；岗位”，指收发清单里写到、被记下的那一个，到 1985 年这一个成了收发清单里的一行。
post 意为“邮政之事”，邮差六月写道，整件事的邮政之事是一处邮局和三个星期的记下。
post 意为“邮政；岗位”，我记得的是收发清单里记下过的那一个，1987 年送完了，至今仍被说成邮局里最安静的一个。
post 为抽象总称，母亲 1989 年说，邮政是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的邮政。
